[nested_closed_interval_theorem] Nested Closed Interval Theorem

Whether it’s an nested interval or a linearly ordered chain of nested intervals, linear order implies monotonicity of interval endpoints. For the set of smaller endpoints, use supremum ; for the set of larger endpoints, use infimum , obtaining with that the intersection of the nested closed intervals is the closed interval . can be understood as the minimum element of the linearly ordered chain of nested intervals

[closed_interval_intersection_theorem]

In fact, it’s sufficient that the smaller endpoints of the closed interval family are all the larger endpoints to conclude the intersection is non-empty

[closed_interval_net_theorem] Closed interval net intersection non-empty

Proof

Closed interval network ==> The small endpoints of the closed interval family are all large endpoints

The reverse direction “the small endpoints of the closed interval family are all large endpoints ==> interval net” is not true.
